title: Traffic acceptance criteria tally & sprint matrix
summary: Compact working sheet to validate traffic acceptance criteria, map KPIs to sprint owners, and surface gating decisions for first-wave rollouts.
content:
Purpose:
- Create a tight, action-oriented tally of acceptance criteria for traffic + capacity so product, infra, and SRE can sign off quickly for go/no-go and staged ramping.
- Combine KPI targets, scenario probes, and owner + sprint commitments in one glanceable matrix.

Quick status (snapshot):
- Beta cohort readiness: partial (feature flags in place, but canary automation missing)
- KPI gaps: expected p95 latency for text-gen vs measured currently at 1.8x target during a 10QPS load test
- Blocking risk: KV-cache cold-start regression in latest runtime build (serving-runtime/issue-512)

KPI targets (production acceptance):
- Latency p50 target: 70ms (current baseline: 48ms)
- Latency p95 target: 220ms (current baseline: 400ms under 10QPS stress) -> FAIL
- Error rate (5xx) target: <= 0.05% (current: 0.2% during spike test) -> FAIL
- Token cost/unit: budget <= $0.0009/token (forecast sheet linked)
- Availability SLO: 99.95% for initial phase
- Throughput baseline for phase 1: 20 QPS sustained per model route with burst to 80 QPS

Acceptance criteria checklist (tally style):
- [ ] Canary deploy automation configured (owner: Ben Torres) -> Jira JIRA-380 (due: 2026-03-05)
- [x] Feature flagging path validated for 5 cohorts (owner: Maya Singh) -> notes: rollback button present
- [ ] Autoscale policy review complete with SRE for GPU pools (owner: Liam O'Connor) -> blocked by capacity plan
- [ ] KV cache warmup script in release (owner: eng-serving-runtime) -> failing on mixed-quant models
- [x] Observability dashboards created: per-route latency + cost (owner: product-ops)

Traffic scenarios and gating rules:
- Scenario A (happy path): gradual ramp to 20 QPS over 48h; gate: p95 < 250ms and 5xx < 0.1%
- Scenario B (surge): 4x traffic spike for 10 minutes; gate: error rate does not exceed 1% and fallback to cheaper model triggers below 2s
- Scenario C (region failover): shift to secondary region; gate: median latency rise < 60% and no token leak observed

Sprint matrix (owners + commitments):
- Sprint Wk1 (owner: Ben): canary infra + rollback hook; tasks: automated smoke tests, rollout script refinements
- Sprint Wk2 (owner: Maya): final user-experience gating, feature flag choreography, customer comms template
- Sprint Wk3 (owner: Liam + eng-sre): autoscale tuning, GPU warm pool provisioning, runbook drill
- Sprint Wk4 (owner: product-ops): KPI signoff, post-rollout sampling plan, cost monitoring alerts

Triage playbook (if any gate fails):
1) Move to limited cohort (0.1% of traffic) and snapshot traces -> immediate
2) Activate fallback policy to a cheaper/compatible model variant -> within 60s
3) Escalate to oncall SRE and product-ops lead -> within 5 minutes
4) Revert to last-known-good model version if errors persist > 15 minutes

Operational checks before go (preflight):
- Smoke test matrix: auth, model routing, stream flow, cancellation, cost-metering
- Data plane audit: keys, logs, sampling rate verified for compliance
- Customer opt-in UX: clear messaging + opt-out toggle tested

Risk register + mitigations (short form):
- Risk: KV-cache cold starts -> Mitigation: staged warmup + prefetch script, explicit cache-seed job (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- Risk: Cost blowout if quantization misconfig -> Mitigation: throttle per-customer token rate, cost-alert threshold (owner: product-ops)
- Risk: Observability blind spots for rerouted requests -> Mitigation: add trace tags for routing-policy and variant (owner: observability)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What is the official fallback model family for low-tier customers? (product to decide by 2026-03-01)
- Approve temporary increase in burst capacity for first 72h (finance signoff required)
- Agreement on sampling rate for fidelity checks (SRE + Research)

Action items (short):
- Ben: finish canary automation + link PR (github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts/pull/87) (due 2026-03-05)
- Maya: finalize cohort comms + preflight checklist for support reps (due 2026-03-03)
- Liam: run two more 24h soak tests with different seq-length distributions (due 2026-03-07)
- Product-ops: run KPI signoff meeting with exec stakeholders (tentative 2026-03-09)

Notes / context / references:
- Reference load test report: shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/load-tests/2026-02-20-summary.pdf
- Related playbook: confluence: traffic-modeling-playbook (linked_artifacts above)
- Slack discussions: #prodops (thread ts: 1678901200) -> see JIRA-380 for detailed comments

Quick win checklist (things we can do in <48h):
- Add a simple acceptance toggle to console to put traffic into cohort 0.1% (owner: developer-experience)
- Increase alert granularity on 5xx by model route (owner: observability)
- Wire a cost burn dashboard widget for the rollout page (owner: product-ops)

Sign-off criteria (for product-ops):
- All critical acceptance criteria checked OR documented compensating controls
- Exec stakeholder (VP Product) + SRE oncall have acknowledged and signed the runbook
- Financial guardrails approved for first wave

End notes: This is a living tally. Keep updates minimal and date-stamped on each change. Prefer incremental checks over large all-or-nothing gates.

Change log (brief):
- 2025-11-06 created by Aisha Patel
- 2026-02-10: added surge scenario gating (Maya Singh)
- 2026-02-28: updated KPI measured baselines after 10QPS test (Liam O'Connor)
